items.request: Walk through the import lines at the top of the main app file of the Datasette repository and group them into families: concurrency, templating, signing, database, views, plugins. For each family, say in one plain sentence what the app uses it for.
items.why: A parts list is a definition to read and group, so a short written card with a table fits.

items.request: Explain the async and thread imports in the main app file of Datasette, and the default of 3 threads for running SQL. Show that one world runs the request with asyncio while a thread pool runs blocking SQLite work.
items.why: Pairs the imports with the default value in one short reading.

items.request: Explain the template-related imports in the Datasette main app file: which loaders are imported and why a choice loader exists, so that search order across template folders lets plugins and users override defaults.
items.why: Background idea, best as a brief reading.

items.request: Ask one multiple-choice question about Datasette's main app file: which imports (a third-party serializer library and the secrets module) back signed values and API tokens, and what is the default of the setting that allows signed tokens? Give feedback.
items.why: A quick check that the learner can find the signing pieces.

items.request: Draw the Datasette app object as a hub: imported view classes (index, row, table) as routing targets, and the plugin manager dispatching hooks to plugins.
items.why: The hub-and-targets shape is structural and best seen.

items.request: Write a small Python example mirroring Datasette's settings table: a namedtuple Setting with name, default and help, entries like default page size 100 and SQL time limit 1000 ms, then print each default.
items.why: Lets the learner see the tuple shape and real default values.
